description: 47 Antriksh Legacy India is a space-science innovation team led by Parth Kumar Rai from India. We are passionate about aerospace engineering, planetary science, lunar + Martian exploration, satellites, astronomy and human spaceflight. Our goal is to investigate scientific questions, explore NASA's open data and research, and present creative, evidence-based ideas. We value curiosity, critical thinking and innovation, and believe every discovery begins with a question. DREAM • INNOVATE • EXPLORE!
summary:
Have you ever wondered what happens to spacecraft after their missions are over? We often celebrate successful space missions, but rarely talk about the machines and equipment that remain behind on other worlds.

ABANDONED BUT NOT FORGOTTEN is my attempt to explore that side of space exploration. Through this project, I look at some of the machines left on the Moon and Mars, including Apollo's lunar equipment, the Viking landers, Spirit, Opportunity, InSight and Ingenuity.

I wanted to understand why these machines were sent, what they achieved and what happened to them after their missions ended.

While researching this topic, I also discovered that not everything left behind is completely useless. Some equipment still helps scientists, while other objects remain as important reminders of past missions.

For me, these machines are more than abandoned equipment. They represent human curiosity, engineering and our desire to explore places beyond Earth.
details:
WHY I CHOSE THIS TOPIC

Whenever we hear about space exploration, we usually focus on new discoveries, successful landings and exciting missions. But there is another part of this story that often goes unnoticed: the machines that remain on other worlds after their work is finished.

I wanted to explore what happens to these machines and why they still matter.

EXPLORING THE MOON

The first part of my project focuses on the Moon. I have included equipment from the Apollo missions, such as the Lunar Module descent stages, Lunar Roving Vehicles and Lunar Laser Retroreflectors.

These objects tell us about the early days of human exploration and the technology that helped astronauts explore the lunar surface.

EXPLORING MARS

The next part takes us to Mars. It covers missions and machines such as Viking 1 and 2, Spirit, Opportunity, InSight, Perseverance and Ingenuity.

Each of these missions had a different purpose. Some studied the Martian surface, some investigated its interior, and others helped us understand whether Mars may once have supported conditions suitable for life.

WHY DO THESE MACHINES FALL SILENT?

Space is a difficult environment for machines. Extreme temperatures, radiation, dust, ageing components and power limitations can affect their ability to operate.

This part of the project explains some of the reasons why spacecraft eventually stop working or lose contact with Earth.

THE IMPORTANCE OF PRESERVING SPACE HERITAGE

I also wanted to highlight that these objects are part of human history. Future explorers should understand their importance and avoid unnecessarily disturbing historic landing sites.

WHAT I HOPE PEOPLE TAKE AWAY

Through this project, I hope readers look at space exploration from a slightly different perspective. A mission does not become unimportant just because its spacecraft stops working.

The discoveries, achievements and stories behind these machines continue to be valuable.

Our journey into space is not only about the worlds we reach, but also about the footprints we leave behind.
